sentences.text: Nemacanthus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish.
Its name means 'to distribute spine' and it belongs to the family Palaeospinacidae.
The genus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus was described by Agassiz in 1837.
Scientists have recorded 83 fossil occurrences of this group.
The oldest known fossils date to the Middle Permian period.
Remains have been found in the Wordian age Khuff Formation of Oman.
The species Nemacanthus elegans lived during the Triassic period in Idaho, United States.
The genus existed from the Wordian to the Toarcian, spanning 266.9 to 174.7 million years ago.
